message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering public vulnerability information newly reported or materially updated in the last 24 hours for the scheduled July 17, 2026 IST run. Confirmed relevant findings were found for SonicWall, NGINX, Google Chrome, Zoom, and Ubuntu.

**Finding 1: SonicWall SMA 1000 Series zero-day vulnerabilities**

- Product: SonicWall / Dell SonicWall SMA 1000 Series
- Issue: CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410 / SNWLID-2026-0008
- Severity: Critical for CVE-2026-15409 (CVSS 10.0); High for CVE-2026-15410 (CVSS 7.2)
- Description: SonicWall reports a server-side request forgery issue and a remote code execution issue affecting SMA 1000 Series 12.4.3 and 12.5.0 firmware branches. SonicWall states these vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild, and Rapid7 updated its technical analysis on July 16.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes SonicWall and Dell SonicWall, and SMA 1000 is a SonicWall secure remote access product.
- Source: SonicWall product notice: https://www.sonicwall.com/support/notices/product-notice-sma-1000-series-affected-by-multiple-vulnerabilities/kA1VN000001nv6D0AQ ; Rapid7 analysis updated July 16: https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-rapid7-mdr-team-discovers-new-sonicwall-sma1000-zero-days-being-actively-exploited-cve-2026-15409-cve-2026-15410/

**Finding 2: NGINX vulnerabilities disclosed by F5/NGINX**

- Product: Nginx
- Issue: CVE-2026-42533, CVE-2026-60005, and CVE-2026-56434
- Severity: Major for CVE-2026-42533; Medium for CVE-2026-60005 and CVE-2026-56434, per the NGINX advisory listing
- Description: NGINX lists newly published vulnerabilities involving map/regex handling, ngx_http_slice_module memory disclosure/restart conditions, and ngx_http_ssi_module use-after-free/over-read conditions. F5 advisory snippets show the three advisories were published July 15, and NVD shows at least CVE-2026-42533 was modified July 16.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Nginx, and the NGINX advisory page explicitly names NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus affected version ranges.
- Source: NGINX security advisories: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html ; NVD CVE-2026-42533: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42533

**Finding 3: Google Chrome Stable Channel security update**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: Chrome 150.0.7871.128/.129 desktop update and related Chrome browser security fixes
- Severity: Mixed; Google lists Critical, High, Medium, and Low browser fixes in the July 16 release notes
- Description: Google released Chrome Stable updates for Windows, Mac, and Linux on July 16. The same release page lists Chrome browser security fixes including critical and high-severity issues such as use-after-free, heap buffer overflow, type confusion, and insufficient validation flaws.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Google Chrome.
- Source: Google Chrome Releases, July 16, 2026: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/

**Finding 4: Zoom Workplace for Windows improper input validation**

- Product: Zoom
- Issue: ZSB-26014 / CVE-2026-53412
- Severity: Critical, per Zoom; third-party reporting cites CVSS 9.8
- Description: Zoom’s security bulletin list shows CVE-2026-53412 for Zoom Workplace for Windows, published July 14 and updated July 15. Public reporting on July 16 says the flaw could allow unauthenticated account takeover via network access.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Zoom, and Zoom Workplace is the main Zoom desktop client family.
- Source: Zoom Security Bulletins: https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/security-bulletin/ ; The Hacker News coverage, July 16: https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/zoom-patches-critical-windows-flaw-that.html

**Finding 5: Ubuntu Security Notices published July 16**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: USN-8557-1 Authlib vulnerabilities, USN-8556-1 Ruby vulnerabilities, USN-8555-1 Ubuntu Advantage Tools vulnerabilities, and USN-8554-1 NTFS-3G vulnerabilities
- Severity: Varies by notice; the notices listing does not provide one overall severity for the batch
- Description: Canonical published multiple Ubuntu Security Notices on July 16 for supported Ubuntu releases, fixing security issues in official Ubuntu packages.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu, and these are official Ubuntu security notices for maintained releases.
- Source: Ubuntu Security Notices listing: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Possible matches needing review**

**Fortinet FortiSandbox KEV update**

- CISA added Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-39808 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 16, and NVD/CVE enrichment was updated the same day. This was not included as a confirmed finding because Products.txt lists Fortigate/FortiOS, while the affected product is FortiSandbox / FortiSandbox PaaS, a separate Fortinet product line.
- Source: NVD CVE-2026-39808: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-39808 ; Fortinet FG-IR-26-100: https://fortiguard.fortinet.com/psirt/FG-IR-26-100

**VMware Avi Load Balancer report**

- Public reporting on July 16 discusses CVE-2026-47865 in VMware Avi Load Balancer. This was not included as a confirmed finding because Products.txt lists VMware ESXi, VMware vCenter, and VMware Tools, not Avi Load Balancer.
- Source: Malwarebytes summary: https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/bugs/2026/07/security-updates-available-for-adobe-chrome-firefox-vmware-and-zoom

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for SonicWall SMA 1000 because the vendor and Rapid7 describe active exploitation. NGINX and Chrome should also be prioritized where exposed or widely deployed. Zoom and Ubuntu updates should move through normal accelerated patch channels based on deployment footprint.
